title: Client visual checkpoint — Home and Onboarding

decisions.BASE-01: Stacked on PR29, including PR23–29. No rollback to the older f0507c5 design catalog.
decisions.NAV-01: Keep five real Client routes including /client/program. No invented account route. Actual Client identity; staff-only Coach return stays in the account area.
decisions.STATE-01: Keep existing reads and Onboarding -> Week Zero action selection. Actual program component reports publication independently; remove contradictory unavailability text on the checkpoint Home only.
decisions.DATA-01: No extra Week Zero summary query or fictitious values. Keep a link to the existing Client Week Zero.
decisions.LEGACY-01: No additional migration or claim of Legacy feature parity.
decisions.PREF-01: Existing locale and unit data preserved; no preference reset/storage. Existing local fonts/logo reused byte-identically.
decisions.SAVE-01: Existing save/Continue/submit, idempotency, conflicts, read-only and unsaved-navigation guards retained. Document links from long questionnaire preserve navigation warnings.

deviations: Desktop/mobile questionnaire references show different states; both states remain supported at all sizes.
Mobile navigation combines horizontally accessible steps and labelled native section selector; no swipe-only navigation.
Long section introductions remain available behind an explicit About this section disclosure, placing the first field above the fold.
Save/Continue controls remain in normal flow to avoid covering fields, errors or mobile keyboards.
Current program access and staff-only portal switch retained despite their absence in the older visual references.
Today, Week Zero, program detail, Coach and Auth not visually generalized before human checkpoint validation.

assets.processing: WebP quality85, desktop2172px/mobile1086px, CSS responsive crop; master retained in original handoff
WebP quality85,720px wide; master retained in original handoff
No duplication: existing local assets match supplied hashes

acceptance: Technical verification does not replace Cavalier5/Max visual acceptance. No full WCAG certification, physical mobile keyboard test or new feature claims.
